questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
So the buzzer or light stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They become better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should always sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Follow closely behind any vehicle ahead of you.
Keep a two-second following distance behind any vehicle ahead of you.
Pull over on the right side and stop.

questions.explanation: Slow down and stay alert in work zones to keep workers and drivers safe. Keep a 4-second following distance, do not change lanes, and be patient around workers.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your freeway exit?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, or swerve across lanes on the highway. Do not cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What documents must you show if stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle when you drive. You must show all three documents if stopped.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of hazards ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they take.
They do not have full control of their bodies, minds, or vehicles.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not have full control of their bodies, minds, or vehicles.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The road has many curves ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. You must slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign, which is 35 mph.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both effects stronger. Driving after alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Driving after both together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: Driving ability can be harmed by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving needs you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all hurt your driving ability.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers act angry, move away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You must change how you drive when weather changes suddenly.
You should slow down in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: If you see a horse and rider on the road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn them.
Drive next to the horse to help it adjust to vehicles.
Speed up to pass the horse quickly.

questions.explanation: Drive slowly around any animal on the road to avoid scaring it. For horses, slow down, move away, and don't use your horn. Animals can be unpredictable and may run into your path.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb because:

options.text: It is only needed if other cars are nearby.
It is good practice and the law requires it.
You only need to signal during the move, not before.
It is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Signal before you pull away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times while driving.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.
